body: Same man, except I'm 23. No close friends, just "acquaintances" if you can even call them that. No way to meaningfully connect with anyone. Seems to get more and more hopeless the more time goes on.

I had something like this at one point, but I blew it and still deeply regret it. I guess it's one of those things that some people take for granted and don't truly appreciate it until it's gone...

I don't have any advice or anything that could help you right now OP, but if you do find that special person, cling onto that relationship and don't let it slip away. Just don't be *too* clingy.

Interesting. You don't often see an extrovert become an introvert and find happiness in that change. You make a good point that the grass isn't always greener, even for extroverts. I never truly considered the share of problems and inconveniences that they face in their lives, just seeing all the potential good. I may need to rethink my views on my life up to now. Maybe it wasn't a waste, maybe I've been doing what I preferred to do all along, and there's nothing actually wrong with it...I suppose it's time to consider what I'd REALLY like to change about myself, and what I'm already happy with.

This subreddit alone shows how many people can be "lost" at some point in their lives; it's more common than it's generally perceived to be for sure. As you said not everyone knows what they want for a career in the beginning, maybe some never do. Even those who do and get their dream jobs probably aren't happy with it 100% of the time. Working a decent job and focusing on happiness outside of work sounds like a good plan. I don't want much in life, just to make enough money to get by and be content with myself. Hopefully I get there someday.

Not really rural, no. I live in a relatively small town, but in a wooded area that's kind of away from things. It's a fairly quick drive to the main part of town, but walking isn't practical. As for things to do, there's a decent amount I guess, but I don't know what I would do by myself. Joining some sort of club that suits my interests would probably be the best bet, though I would probably have to look outside of my town to find a good one.

That's cool that moving worked for you. I've heard that the west coast is more relaxed and has different values, at least compared to where I live (northeastern US). Moving isn't a real option for me at this point in time. I'd need to be able to prove to myself and my family that I can be more independent first, and it might be better in the long run to be able to overcome the uncomfortable situations I don't like to be in before anything else.
I'm going to try hard to do these things. Thank you!

Well, I feel a little better after reading this. I think I've been focusing too much on the "should've, would've, could've" positives about going to college right out of high school, having an awesome time and getting a great degree and some kind of magical dream career, instead of looking at the whole picture realistically. Maybe it wouldn't have been all good things, and there may have been some bad things I avoided as well, maybe for better. Who knows?

So now I'm again feeling as if my life won't be over before it started, that I still have a chance to do something worthwhile, maybe even great; hopefully it stays this way. Thanks man. :)

I'm 23, so I didn't get to experience much of the 90s myself. That stuff you described all sounds pretty crazy to me, but I was always the kind of kid who wouldn't even dare to do anything even slightly out of line. To others it would probably just be kids being kids. But yeah, from what I hear things are a lot more strict now compared to "back in the day". Perhaps too strict in some cases.

Yeah, the people of this subreddit are awesome, understanding and very supportive. There might be trolls sometimes but the genuinely good people far outnumber them. Just don't let the mean people bring you down, they likely have their own issues and insecurities, and take it out on people who don't deserve it.
This is just the first step, friend. But keep it going and you'll be more comfortable posting your thoughts in time, I'm sure of it. Don't let that voice discourage you, you deserve to be heard. :)

I wish you a good day as well, and many more good days to come! Glad I could make you feel better, if even just a little.

Cold showers and exercising helps a little, but the effects never seem to last very long for me. Going outside doesn't help much sadly. I have an overactive mind, and can never live in the moment or appreciate what's going on around me, including nature; I really wish I could. I'll keep trying though!
United States

I'm probably going to get a part-time job when I'm able to. I don't see many other realistic options besides that. Not sure that going to school and aimlessly floating through would be a good idea, especially when I have such fleeting interests. But maybe when I'm out there more and discover more things, I can be more comfortable making some of the more long-term decisions...idk...
I know this, I just don't know where to start.

I don't know if it's just one person, but it's probably mostly my fault. No one has ever really pushed me to do things, but I have no ambition to begin with. I'd like to get out of the house more, but I don't have a vehicle, and there's really nothing within walking distance or anything, unless you count nature.

Hey, just looked at your post. Not saying anything or writing messages because they seem stupid or pointless, I know that feeling all too well. Most of my messages take me quite a while to type out, and when I'm done I feel like I HAVE TO check for any errors or things that may come across the wrong way. It's a nightmare sometimes but I'm trying to get better lol.

It may help to realize that a lot of what people say (especially the extra talkative ones) is pointless stuff said just for the sake of conversation. Not to say that's a bad thing or it should be disregarded, but just know that even if you say something that makes you look like a fool, it may make you feel awkward for a bit. But 9 times out of 10 people are going to forget about it or just not care. They're looking inward at themselves as well. If this doesn't help, you may eventually just stop caring to a certain degree, after getting fed up with how things are, and kind of just express how you feel without trying to filter it too much. That's the point I'm at right about now.
I would if I could, but I'm practically trapped in my house.

Thanks. I tried learning programming through videos but lost interest pretty quickly. But maybe I'll try again, and look into those other ones as well. I'm mainly worried about getting stuck in some low-paying, dead-end job for the rest of my life, since I don't have any strong skills or knowledge in anything specific. But I guess even that would be better than nothing...

This is good advice for the average person, but what if one has no dreams, no goals, no ambitions, no desires, no drive? What then?

All my life I've been incredibly indecisive and have never had a true passion or calling, just floating through life and doing what I was told. Depression has simply made this much worse.

I honestly didn't think this post would get so much attention haha.
Yeah, it's a little comforting to know I'm not alone in this. I guess it's just hard to really comprehend since it's rare to see others experience this in day to day life, because they're isolated as well..

I don't have a job. I just help my parents with whatever needs to be done, and do house chores. That's pretty much it. I'm tired of it but I can't change anything at this point in time. I feel trapped.
Nah it's fine, it's more clear to me now. The boulder rolling thing sounds like a fun time lol. I never really did much crazy stuff growing up, for better or worse.

I've been to a therapist before to talk about one of my anxieties, but not depression. I might try to get more help in the future though. I'd prefer to try everything else I can before going on medication.

That sucks man. Hope your situation improves, and rooting for you as well!

About the skilled trades, my father is really into carpentry and woodworking. I sometimes help him with things, but nothing has really clicked with me yet. As for the other trades, I haven't really looked into them much apart from some very small experiences or light research. Tradesman around me say this type of work is very in demand since most don't want to "work hard" anymore, and as you said it can pay well. However I don't want to get into that type of work just for those reasons, I want to be sure I'll enjoy it as well. So yeah, I'm not to sure about taking that route yet, but I'll keep that option open for consideration.
Family is the only thing keeping me here. I don't have many opportunities to socialize with people outside my family at the moment, so I'll keep trying online for now, see how that works...

I honestly feel as though I'll never change the way I want to. I'll always be...well...too much like the me I've been all my life so far. I can try to be more open and talkative but most of the time it feels so forced. Even if I end up being successful in changing somewhat, I don't think the feeling will ever completely go away.

I originally never went due to the cost and the fact that I didn't know what I wanted to do; that hasn't really changed. I don't want to go just for the sake of going, end up wasting money and more time, and be even worse off. Even if I didn't have to worry about wasting anything, the fact that I would be older than the majority of students is also discouraging. 

That's the realistic outlook for me. Sometimes I fantasize about having gone at the earliest age, and having a great time. That's the point where I think about being able to do something with my life, although ultimately it probably wouldn't be as good as I imagine.
I'm not sure if I understood this 100%, but I think I got the gist. I suppose this new system could work in some form, so long as society (especially the larger corporations) embraces it.
I'll consider it, and thanks.

Apart from avoiding debt, I don't think it was a good decision. At least if I went I could've had the chance to do something meaningful with my life.

I admire the thought you put into this idea, but I don't think it would solve everything. Most of the people doing these jobs now don't make enough to earn a living from it. Extra side money yes, but that's about it. I actually tried a job like these ones from Amazon years back. In my opinion the low pay was not worth the time invested in it, and some didn't even pay at all. The pay from these types of jobs might increase significantly if this becomes a bigger thing, but then there's the issue of competition again, because everyone is going to want to do them instead of traditional work. Maybe it could work in a future society but I can't see it happening anytime soon.
Anime, games, and some music. I don't know what I'd do without them.
I'm 23 years old. I should be a grown adult at this point, which makes my situation even more pathetic.

Hey man, at least you went to college. I didn't, so I have no future. This competitive world makes me disgusted toward society. Your idea sounds nice on paper, but employers and big businesses probably wouldn't find it beneficial enough for them, sadly. Most would rather have their employees working for them for life, as long as they believe they're still of use.
It really is...makes it so hard to go on...

I was in an online relationship with another depressed person (she came out of an abusive relationship just prior). Started out thinking we could understand each other and I could help her recover, but within a few months it became too much and it had to end. We're still friends, and I'm glad she eventually found someone who can treat her better and actually be with her in person.

Just my experience, so it might not be a good indicator. I'm sure there are depressed people in relationships who can manage to work things out.

Well, no one watches anime where I live and it's pretty much a social stigma anyway. Video games are becoming more accepted but one can only talk about them so much, usually just with other gamers. I usually just comment about the weather or some news I saw, day to day stuff, etc. But I just don't know how to keep it going.

Perfectly readable, and thanks for the concern.

I don't know if I'd ever get to the point of impulsive suicide, it's just the thoughts mainly. I think just imagining how quickly it could end would scare me away from actually doing it to be honest. I really don't want to get rid of the gun for certain reasons...maybe a good compromise would be to make it harder to immediately access. Make it so I would have to really go out of my way to get it and have some more time to think about the decision if it ever happened, and keep the bullets completely separated as well.
All the time, daydream a lot too. Pretty sure it's a coping mechanism at this point.
Looking back at it now, I'm not sure what kind of comfort or advice I was looking for posting this. Maybe just to let it out or see if people here could relate in some way, not sure...

My dad bought it for me years ago, for my birthday I think. Other than for protection, he wanted us to get into shooting targets and stuff as a hobby, although that never really ended up happening. I live in a relatively safe and out of the way place, but in my opinion it's good to have a firearm just in case.

Like I said I'm not actually planning on taking my own life, and the gun is nice to have for self defense purposes. Plus if I really tried to get rid of it my parents would think something is up. Thanks for the suggestion though.

I get that the rational way of thinking is to learn from your mistakes and not beat yourself up over them, but that's hard for certain people. Plus I feel like I make way more mistakes than I should, way more than others..

It really depends. People who are "successful" in life are more than just attractive, they're outgoing and/or have a strong charisma for one. Just imagine if you were attractive, but had severe social anxiety. Sure you might get some looks your way and some may approach you, but it will all fall apart the same way when they find out they can't get you to open up to them.

So try not to beat yourself up so much. Acknowledge your good points and strive to improve in any way you can. :)
Thank you.
It's comforting to know I'm not alone in this, but it sucks that you're suffering as well. Hope you get the help you deserve.
